findings.title: Public helpers removed from mark_failed without compatibility shims or confirmed import updates
findings.body: This refactor deletes several module-level symbols from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed: `mark_failed_threshold` (renamed `try_incident_threshold` in incidents.py), `create_issue_platform_occurrence` (renamed `create_incident_occurrence` in incident_occurrence.py), `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and the `SimpleCheckIn` TypedDict (moved to sentry.monitors.types). None of the old names are re-exported from mark_failed. Any other module, test, or downstream import that does `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import mark_failed_threshold / create_issue_platform_occurrence / get_failure_reason / get_monitor_environment_context / SimpleCheckIn` will raise ImportError at load time, breaking the import graph. The PR only changes these 4 files, so search all call sites and update them (or leave thin aliases in mark_failed) before merging.

findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context builds a modified config copy but returns the original, so schedule_type display is lost
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context() copies the monitor config into the local `config`, replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with `monitor.get_schedule_type_display()`, but then returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the mutated `config`. The `get_schedule_type_display()` conversion is therefore dead code and the event context ships the raw schedule_type value. This was carried over verbatim from the old mark_failed.py, but since this file is newly added it should be fixed here: return the modified `config`.

findings.title: get_failure_reason docstring examples do not match the produced strings
findings.body: The docstring claims outputs like "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected", but the implementation joins only the bare status labels ("missed", "timeout", "error") via get_text_list, so the actual mixed result is "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", and the singular branch can only return one of the SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP strings ("A missed/error/timeout check-in was detected"), never "A failed check-in was detected". The docstring should reflect the real output (and "humam readible" is misspelled).
